h1:
Where to stay in
Khao San & Old City
intro: Khao San and the Old City (Rattanakosin/Phra Nakhon) is the part of Bangkok you can spend a whole day exploring on foot. The Grand Palace, Wat Phra Kaew, and Wat Pho are all a short walk apart, while Khao San Road and Soi Rambuttri pack in cheap guesthouses, bars, and street food. The one thing to know before you book: no train line runs through here, so getting to other districts means catching the express boat at Phra Athit pier or grabbing a taxi. The picks below run from party dorms to riverside boutiques.

blocks.html: Short answer: Khao San and the Old City put you within walking distance of the Grand Palace, Wat Pho, and Khao San Road itself, all on foot. The catch is there's no BTS or MRT here, so you rely on the Chao Phraya express boat or a taxi/Grab to reach the rest of town. Beds range from a few-hundred-baht backpacker dorm to riverside boutiques in the low thousands.

blocks.text: Recommended hotels in Khao San & Old City

items.name: Mad Monkey Bangkok
items.meta: ★ 2-star · Best for: Party crowd · meeting people · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A well-known Mad Monkey backpacker hostel about an 8-minute walk from Khao San Road, with a pool, bar, and rooftop for socialising. Dorms have privacy curtains and personal sockets. Great for solo travellers who want to meet people, but it's adults-only and gets loud at night, so light sleepers may want to look elsewhere.

items.name: Sloth Hostel Khaosan
items.meta: ★ 2-star · Best for: Budget · quiet seekers · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A small, clean-lined hostel on Soi Kraisi, about a 5-minute walk to Khao San Road. The draw is how quiet and tidy it is, plus a rooftop to relax on. Dorms come with privacy curtains, reading lights, and personal sockets, and breakfast is included. A good fit for backpackers who want a calmer vibe than the party hostels. No pool.

items.name: Royal Rattanakosin Hotel
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: Value · near the Grand Palace · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A large, long-running hotel of about 300 rooms, roughly a 5-minute walk from Khao San Road and under a kilometre from the Grand Palace and Wat Pho. It has a pool and on-site restaurants. Rooms are clean and good value for an Old City address, though the building and decor feel dated, so don't expect anything modern.

items.name: Lamphu Tree House
items.meta: ★ 3-star · Best for: Couples · canal-side calm · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A small boutique hotel beside the Banglamphu canal, about a 15-minute walk to Khao San Road. The selling points are an outdoor pool and an easygoing canal-side restaurant. Rooms have a fridge, TV, and air-con. Reviews praise the friendly staff and a setting quieter than the middle of Khao San, making it a nice pick for couples or anyone wanting a calmer base.

items.name: Nouvo City Hotel
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: Families · two pools · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A modern boutique hotel on Samsen Road in the Ban Phan Thom area, about a 15-minute walk to Khao San Road. It has two swimming pools, a spa, a gym, and on-site restaurants, and scores around 9.0 in reviews. The spacious, clean rooms and family-friendly facilities are the highlight. The kitchen is halal-certified, so it also suits Muslim travellers.

items.name: Villa Bangkok (formerly Villa Phra Sumen)
items.meta: ★ 3-star · Best for: Couples · restored-house charm · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A small 29-suite boutique set in two restored old buildings on Phra Sumen Road, about a 10-minute walk to Khao San Road. Suites have high ceilings, wooden floors, and a mix of contemporary and classic Thai furnishings, plus there's an outdoor pool and a small garden. It suits couples who prefer the feel of a restored house over a big hotel.

items.name: Riva Surya Bangkok
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: River views · riverside pool · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A 68-room riverside boutique on Phra Athit Road, right by the Phra Athit pier and about a 15-minute walk to Khao San Road. The highlights are a riverside pool, a terrace for watching the Chao Phraya go by, and restaurants with a view. It scores around 9.5 in reviews and is the top-end choice in this area, ideal for couples or anyone who wants a river view in the Old City.

faq.q: Is it hard to get around from Khao San without a BTS station?
faq.a: It takes a little planning, since no BTS or MRT runs through here. The popular option is the Chao Phraya express boat from Phra Athit pier down to Sathorn, where you can connect to the BTS, or just take a taxi/Grab. For Don Muang or Suvarnabhumi airports, a car is easiest. The Old City temples themselves are all within comfortable walking distance.

faq.q: Is Khao San Road noisy, and which room should I pick?
faq.a: The heart of Khao San Road and Soi Rambuttri has bars open late, so expect noise into the early hours. If you don't sleep easily, ask for a room facing inward or away from the main street, or choose a place set back a little, like the Phra Athit, Banglamphu canal, or Samsen Road side, which are much quieter.

faq.q: Is Khao San good for families, or just for backpackers?
faq.a: Both, depending on where you stay. Khao San Road itself leans toward backpackers and night owls, but the surrounding area has hotels with pools and family rooms, like Nouvo City or Royal Rattanakosin. The upside is being close to the Grand Palace and Wat Pho, which are easy to walk to with kids. Just avoid the rooms right by the bar streets.
